newsitem.title: USA: Wis. business survey sees steady economic growth.
newsitem.headline: Wis. business survey sees steady economic growth.

text.p: Wisconsin Manufacturing & Commerce board members anticipate steady economic growth and low inflation for the coming year, the group announced in survey results released Tuesday.
"Wisconsin's CEOs are very optimistic about the state and national economies," President James Haney said in a statement. "They're adding jobs and expecting growth in the overall economy."

The survey of the non-agricultural group's board of directors found that 41.7 percent planned to add new jobs in the coming year, 47.2 percent anticipated no changes and 8.3 percent expected job cuts.
Nearly 78 percent of respondents expected to see moderate growth in their firms in the coming year and 11.1 percent expect good growth in the next six to 12 months, the survey found.

The executives also said they have offered pay hikes to hourly workers, performance bonuses, education benefits, pensions, flexible scheduling and other incentives as a result of a tight labor market.
More than 83 percent of respondents believed the national inflation rate will remain below five percent in the next year, the survey found.

About 41.7 percent of respondents expected gross domestic product to increase from 2 percent to 2.5 percent in the coming year and another 30.6 percent anticipated gross domestic product to increase 2.6 percent to 3 percent, the survey found.
The group based its results on responses from 36 of 50 board members surveyed in May.
